title: Preity Zinta Is Back — and Kunal Kemmu’s Action-Comedy ‘Vibe’ Might Be Her Best Comeback Vehicle
excerpt: Eight years after her last theatrical release, Preity Zinta returns alongside director-actor Kunal Kemmu in a slick action-comedy dropping September 18.
body:
Preity Zinta hasn’t appeared in a theatrical Bollywood film since 2018. For an entire generation of moviegoers who grew up on Dil Chahta Hai, Kal Ho Naa Ho, and Veer-Zaara, that absence has felt conspicuous. She’s been busy — co-owning Punjab Kings in the IPL, raising her twins in Los Angeles, making the occasional appearance on talk shows — but the big screen? Radio silence.

That ends on September 18, when Vibe hits theatres.

What We Know

Vibe is an action-comedy directed and co-written by Kunal Kemmu, who also stars in one of the lead roles. It’s his second directorial outing after Madgaon Express, which surprised everyone in 2024 with its sharp writing and energetic comedy. The film is produced by Kemmu and Chirag Nihalani under their banner Drongo Films — making it the studio’s debut production — and backed by Amazon MGM Studios.

Joining Kemmu and Zinta are Sparsh Shrivastava (who broke out in Jubilee) and debutant Vanshika Dhir. The first poster shows all four in silhouette against a neon-lit city skyline, bathed in pink and purple — suggesting a slick, urban, after-dark energy.

The plot follows two friends pulled into a high-stakes adventure. Beyond that, the makers are keeping things close to the chest.

Why Preity’s Comeback Matters

Here’s the thing about Preity Zinta: she was never replaced. After she stepped away, nobody filled that exact niche — the actress who could go from dimpled rom-com charm to fierce emotional depth without breaking a sweat. Dil Se and Lakshya proved she could do serious; Salaam Namaste and Kal Ho Naa Ho proved she could do light. No one else quite managed that range.

For NRIs especially, Zinta holds a particular place. She married Gene Goodenough, an American, and has been living in Los Angeles. She’s been one of the most visible Bollywood-to-diaspora bridges — showing up at IPL matches in the US, engaging with fans on social media, raising her kids between two cultures. Her return to acting feels like a homecoming that the diaspora gets in a way Bollywood-inside-India doesn’t quite.

Kemmu’s Directorial Streak

Kunal Kemmu was always a better actor than his filmography suggested — Kalyug, Traffic Signal, and Go Goa Gone showed range, even when the roles didn’t come his way. But his pivot to directing has been revelatory. Madgaon Express proved he could write sharp dialogue and stage comedy with genuine energy.

With Vibe, he’s scaling up: bigger cast, action set pieces, Amazon MGM Studios backing. The fact that he’s directing, writing, producing, and starring suggests enormous confidence — or enormous ambition. Either way, it’s the kind of all-in bet that makes for interesting cinema.

The September Slot

September is traditionally a quiet month at the Indian box office, sandwiched between the Independence Day rush and the Diwali blockbusters. That could work in Vibe’s favour — less competition, more breathing room for a mid-budget action-comedy to find its audience.

For NRIs with Amazon Prime subscriptions, the theatrical-to-streaming pipeline should be fast. September 18 in theatres worldwide, with an OTT window likely by Diwali.

Vibe releases September 18 in theatres via Amazon MGM Studios.
